It's material we haven't put in front of you yet. Total revenue was $7.8 billion, up 92 percent year over year. But look at where it came from.

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — August 24, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with Delaware Life. Three sessions ago, this briefing closed on the argument that in an asset class this opaque, repricing happens through disclosure before default. Here is that mechanism firing, three days later, and it didn't arrive as a missed payment.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — August 24, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with a concession, because it changes an argument this show has been running all week. Across four sessions, we've treated general-partner marks as private equity's soft spot. On Wednesday it was continuation-vehicle prices set by the sponsor itself.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — August 24, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the macro backdrop. Strategic Power has the full version, starting with letters of intent that would convert up to $874 million of CHIPS Act money into equity in six more chip and AI-supply-chain companies. Nothing has closed yet.

episodes.title: Frontier AI Lab Competition — August 25, 2026
episodes.summary: This show has spent a week arguing that the price floor under frontier AI isn't set in San Francisco or Mountain View. It's set in Hangzhou and Beijing, at zero, because free Chinese open weights undercut whatever the American labs charge. In the last ten days, the people setting that floor started charging for it.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — August 25, 2026
episodes.summary: For four briefings running, this program has asked whether Treasury's bond buyback was real duration removal or just a signal. For three, it called oil the one asset still rising in a straight line. Monday answered both questions. Both answers point at plumbing rather than fundamentals. That's the thesis today.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — August 25, 2026
episodes.summary: The industry is on track for its biggest revenue year ever. The story this morning is what that number is made of. This is a repricing, not simply an expansion, and last week's tape suggests equity investors have started to treat that difference as real risk.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — August 25, 2026
episodes.summary: For most of this week, the story in this briefing has been permission. Who, or what, is actually allowed to act. This week one company answered that question twice. Both times the answer was: not the human.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — August 25, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with what a company just gave away for free. Google has transferred its Agent2Agent protocol, known as A2A, into the Agentic AI Foundation, a Linux Foundation-directed standards body. That places A2A alongside Anthropic's Model Context Protocol under one neutral governance roof.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — August 25, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the number this show has been circling all week. Unitree closed Monday at 603.08 yuan. That is more than 40 percent below its opening-day price of 1,100 yuan. Across four trading sessions, roughly 200 billion yuan of market value came off.

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — August 25, 2026
episodes.summary: On Sunday, this show flagged the First Brands confirmation ruling as still pending, and named it first among the things to watch. It came Monday. It came against the debtor.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — August 25, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the macro backdrop. Capital Markets Radar has Treasury escalating its long-bond buyback in stages, and now reportedly weighing funding it out of its General Account cash balance rather than new bill issuance.

episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — August 26, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the tape, briefly, because the tape is not the argument today. Bitcoin traded up to $81,023.41 intraday on August 25th, a three-month high by Bloomberg's own headline, and pulled back the same session into the high seventy-thousands. It's up 22.4 percent on the week.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — August 26, 2026
episodes.summary: For four days running through Monday, this show argued that competitive position in custom AI silicon was being bought rather than won. The currency was Marvell handing Google a warrant on roughly fifty-nine million shares.

episodes.title: AI Products & Applications — August 26, 2026
episodes.summary: For a week now, this show has told you the AI price war lives in the cheap tiers. This week it reached the top of the stack.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — August 26, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with a single afternoon that tells you how nervous this market has gotten about who owns the enterprise software budget.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — August 26, 2026
episodes.summary: Brent has given the entire Iran rally back, and we finally know why. This program called that rally on Sunday — rhetoric-driven, against barrels that were still being pumped, and the most reversible piece of the inflation story on the board — and said on Tuesday that the inflation trigger had gotten materially weaker.

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — August 26, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the Federal Reserve, because today is the deadline in the renewed attempt to remove Governor Lisa Cook. Back on June 29th, the Supreme Court ruled five to four on this fight.

episodes.title: AI in Biopharma R&D — August 26, 2026
episodes.summary: For five straight days this beat has landed on the same conclusion. Every checkable AI win in drug development sits in chemistry or in operations — enrollment rates, filing speed, compound counts — while target selection, the actual choice of what biology to hit, stays unvalidated and unpriced.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — August 26, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with one number pair that reframes the whole liquidity conversation. In the first half of 2026, the slice of the secondaries market that limited partners use to sell grew 4 percent. The slice general partners control grew 35 percent. That is not a rounding difference.
